note:
T-120 (from B-140). The task body is the contract. Context that motivates it: on the night of 2026-08-23/24 the engine could not accept isolated runs (pre-T-114), so the operator landed accepted work manually and closed each run with reject — those runs now read verdict=FAILED and poison seat scorecards (terra, glm52) for work that shipped. Every such run's reject reason begins 'Work ACCEPTED in substance and landed on main' and the landing commit carries the trailer 'Ducklab-Run: <run-id>'.

One addition to the triage deliverables, small and explicit: a re-resolution door — an already-done run whose verdict is FAILED may be re-closed by the operator as resolution=landed with the landing commit sha (recorded as an event, human-attributed), so the past runs can be backfilled once the state exists. No automatic pattern-matching migration; the operator names each run.

Keep scope tight: resolution=landed on close and re-close, sha stored bidirectionally, scorecard/report math treats landed as pass-or-excluded, board renders landed as its own state, and the pinned test (a landed run does not lower the seat's pass rate). (prior accepted SHA: 07696bb7875d4edd5462026d7406640d2f97c79d)

REDO justification: the record believes T-120 accepted because the then_build chain (B-144) committed the REJECTED test as 07696bb onto main; that commit was reset away (never pushed) and the accepted state is a phantom. This run restarts the test stage legitimately.
